ko.title: [마케팅 101 #2] 당신의 제품이 실패한 게 아니라 날씨가 나쁜 거예요

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > 무엇이든 마케팅하려면 먼저 상황을 읽어야 합니다: 당신이 통제할 수 없는 힘(거시환경), 매일 다루는 플레이어(미시환경), 둘 다 결정으로 바꾸는 간단한 틀.

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: 지난 시간에는 마케팅이 특정 고객을 위한 가치 창출에 대한 것이었습니다.

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: 하지만 어떤 회사도 진공 상태에서 가치를 만들지 않습니다.

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: 모든 비즈니스는 자신이 선택하지 않은 날씨 체계 속에 있습니다.

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: 마케터들은 그 날씨를 두 층으로 나눕니다.

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **거시환경**은 큰 것들입니다 — 당신 산업의 모든 회사에 한 번에 영향을 미치는 사회 전체의 힘.

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: 당신은 그것들과 협상할 수 없습니다. 당신이 할 수 있는 것은 그것들이 오는 것을 보는 것뿐입니다.

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **정치/법률** — 규제, 관세, 최저임금법, 데이터 프라이버시 규칙

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
- **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **사회/문화** — 인구통계, 가치관, 습관, 사람들이 정상이라고 생각하는 것

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **기술** — 물건이 만들어지고, 팔리고, 전달되는 방식을 바꾸는 새로운 도구

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: **PESTEL**도 볼 수 있습니다. 이것은 환경과 법률을 자신의 범주로 추가합니다.

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.
segments.tr: **미시환경**은 만질 수 있을 만큼 가까운 것들입니다: 당신의 고객, 당신의 경쟁자, 당신의 공급자, 당신의 유통업자, 그리고 당신의 내부 역량.

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.
segments.tr: 당신은 여전히 이것들을 완전히 통제하지 못하지만, 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다.

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.
You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: 실용적인 접근은 두 층 모두를 실행 가능한 것으로 번역하는 것이고, 그것이 **SWOT**이 하는 일입니다.

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: 위의 행은 당신에 대한 것입니다 — 당신의 회사 내부의 것들.

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: 아래 행은 세상에 대한 것입니다 — 그 밖의 것들.

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: 이 내부/외부의 분류가 사람들이 가장 자주 틀리는 부분입니다.

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).
"Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: "Z세대가 알코올을 덜 마신다"는 기회 또는 위협입니다(외부). 약점이 아닙니다. 아무리 상처를 입혀도요.

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.
It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: 그것은 페어링입니다: 강점을 기회와 매치시키면 전략을 찾았습니다.

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: 약점이 위협 바로 아래에 있으면 당신을 곤경에 빠뜨릴 것을 찾았습니다.

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.
segments.tr: 지난 10년 동안 텍사스와 애리조나의 교외 지역에 퍼진 드라이브스루 커피 체인을 생각해 보세요.

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **정치/법률** — 여러 주에서 최저임금이 올라 가게당 인건비가 증가

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites
segments.tr: - **경제** — 6달러 라떼는 인플레이션이 물릴 때 식료품보다 더 빨리 예산에서 잘려나감

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one
segments.tr: - **사회** — 원격 및 하이브리드 근무가 오전 8시 도심 사무실 러시를 없앴지만, 교외 늦은 오전 시간대를 만듦

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster
segments.tr: - **기술** — 모바일 주문 앱을 사용하면 고객이 도착하기 전에 결제할 수 있어 줄이 더 빨리 움직임

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: 이제 미시환경입니다: 그들의 고객은 통근자와 원격 근무자, 경쟁자는 스타벅스와 괜찮은 아이스 커피를 파는 모든 주유소, 공급자는 변동성 있는 콩 가격의 타격을 받은 커피 수입업자들입니다.

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **강점:** 소형 매장, 식당 없음, 낮은 임대료, 빠른 처리량

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything
segments.tr: - **약점:** 거의 발 고객이 없거나 "앉아서 일하는" 사업이 없어서 한 고객 유형이 모든 것을 짊어짐

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run
segments.tr: - **기회:** 원격 근무자가 여전히 오전 중반 커피 런을 원하는 자동차 의존적인 교외 주택지

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu
segments.tr: - **위협:** 커피 콩 가격 급등과 임금 상승으로 저가 메뉴를 압박

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.
segments.tr: 그들을 페어링하면 전략이 스스로 쓰입니다: 도심이 아닌 주택 밀집 지역 근처의 교외 지역 몰에 소형 매장을 두세요.

segments.src: That's a strength meeting an opportunity.
Meanwhile, the weakness-under-threat combo tells you what to fix — build a loyalty app or a subscription so you're not repricing the menu every time coffee futures jump.
segments.tr: 한편, 약점-위협 콤보는 무엇을 고쳐야 하는지 알려 줍니다 — 로열티 앱이나 구독을 만들어서 커피 선물이 뛸 때마다 메뉴 가격을 다시 책정하지 않도록 하세요.

segments.src: The environment analysis is what decides where the building goes.
segments.tr: 환경 분석이 건물이 어디에 가는지를 결정합니다.

segments.src: 1. The macro environment (PEST: political, economic, social, technological) is the weather you can't control; the micro environment (customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, your own company) is close enough to influence.
segments.tr: 1. 거시환경(PEST: 정치, 경제, 사회, 기술)은 당신이 통제할 수 없는 날씨이고; 미시환경(고객, 경쟁자, 공급자, 유통업자, 당신의 회사)은 영향을 미칠 수 있을 만큼 가깝습니다.

segments.src: 2. SWOT sorts what you found into internal factors (strengths, weaknesses) and external factors (opportunities, threats) — mixing up those two rows is the most common mistake.
segments.tr: 2. SWOT은 당신이 찾은 것을 내부 요소(강점, 약점)와 외부 요소(기회, 위협)로 분류합니다 — 이 두 행을 섞는 것이 가장 흔한 실수입니다.

segments.src: 3. A SWOT list is only useful when you pair the cells: strength + opportunity points to a strategy, weakness + threat points to a risk you need to close.
segments.tr: 3. SWOT 목록은 셀을 페어링할 때만 유용합니다: 강점 + 기회는 전략을 가리키고, 약점 + 위협은 당신이 닫아야 할 위험을 가리킵니다.

segments.src: **1.** A bakery notes: "Our head baker has 20 years of experience."
segments.tr: **1.** 베이커리가 다음과 같이 지적합니다: "우리 수석 베이커는 20년의 경험을 가지고 있습니다."

segments.src: In a SWOT analysis, this belongs in —
**2.** Rising interest rates making customers delay big purchases is part of which layer, and which PEST letter?
segments.tr: **2.** 금리 인상으로 고객이 큰 구매를 미루게 되는 것은 어느 층의 일부이고, PEST의 어느 글자입니까?

segments.src: **3.** O/X: Your main supplier raising prices is part of the macro environment.
segments.tr: **3.** O/X: 당신의 주요 공급자 가격 인상은 거시환경의 일부입니다.

segments.src: - **Macro environment** — broad, society-wide forces (political, economic, social, technological) that affect all firms in an industry and can't be controlled by any one of them.
segments.tr: - **거시환경** — 산업의 모든 회사에 영향을 미치고 그 어느 하나도 통제할 수 없는 광범위한 사회 전체의 힘(정치, 경제, 사회, 기술).

segments.src: - **Micro environment** — the actors closest to the firm — customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, and the company's own resources — that it can influence but not fully control.
segments.tr: - **미시환경** — 회사에 가장 가까운 행위자들 — 고객, 경쟁자, 공급자, 유통업자, 그리고 회사의 자체 자원 — 회사가 영향을 미칠 수 있지만 완전히 통제하지는 못하는.

segments.src: - **PEST / PESTEL** — a checklist for scanning the macro environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological (plus Environmental and Legal in the PESTEL version).
segments.tr: - **PEST / PESTEL** — 거시환경을 스캔하기 위한 체크리스트: 정치, 경제, 사회, 기술(PESTEL 버전에서는 환경과 법률 추가).

segments.src: - **SWOT analysis** — a 2x2 framework sorting internal Strengths and Weaknesses against external Opportunities and Threats to turn environmental scanning into strategy.
segments.tr: - **SWOT 분석** — 내부 강점과 약점을 외부 기회와 위협에 대항하여 분류하여 환경 분석을 전략으로 바꾸는 2x2 프레임워크.

segments.src: - **Environmental scanning** — the ongoing practice of gathering and interpreting information about outside forces, so changes are spotted early rather than after they hit revenue.
segments.tr: - **환경 분석** — 수익에 영향을 미친 후가 아닌 조기에 변화를 감지하기 위해 외부 힘에 대한 정보를 수집하고 해석하는 지속적인 관행.

segments.src: The baker is a resource inside the company, so it's internal and helpful — a strength.
segments.tr: 그 베이커는 회사 내부의 자원이므로 내부이고 도움이 되므로 — 강점입니다.

segments.src: Interest rates are a broad force no single bakery or retailer controls, which makes them macro, and they're the "E" in PEST.
segments.tr: 금리는 어떤 단일 베이커나 소매업자도 통제하지 못하는 광범위한 힘이므로 거시이고, PEST의 "E"입니다.

segments.src: A supplier is a specific party you deal with, negotiate with, and can switch — that's the micro environment.
segments.tr: 공급자는 당신이 다루고, 협상하고, 전환할 수 있는 특정 당사자입니다 — 그것은 미시환경입니다.

segments.src: The macro version of the same problem would be industry-wide commodity inflation.*
segments.tr: 같은 문제의 거시 버전은 산업 전체 상품 인플레이션일 것입니다.*

zh.title: [营销 101 #2] 你的产品没有失败——是天气的错

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > 在营销任何东西之前，你必须"读懂形势"：你无法控制的力量（宏观环境）、你日常打交道的参与者（微观环境），以及一个将两者转化为决策的简单框架。

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: 在上一课中，营销是关于为特定客户创造价值。

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: 但没有公司在真空中创造价值。

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: 每项业务都存在于一个它没有选择的"天气系统"中。

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: 营销人员将这个"天气"分为两层。

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **宏观环境**是大的东西——社会范围的力量，一次影响您行业中的每家公司。

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: 你无法与它们谈判；你只能提前看到它们的到来。

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **政治/法律**——法规、关税、最低工资法、数据隐私规则

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **经济**——利率、通货膨胀、失业率、消费者信心

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **社会/文化**——人口统计、价值观、习惯、人们认为正常的东西

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **技术**——改变东西制造、销售或交付方式的新工具

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: 你也会看到**PESTEL**，它将环境和法律作为自己的类别。
相同的想法，更细致的分类。

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.
segments.tr: **微观环境**是足够接近的东西：你的客户、你的竞争对手、你的供应商、你的分销商和你自己的内部能力。

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.
segments.tr: 你仍然无法完全控制这些，但你可以影响它们。

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.
segments.tr: 你可以与供应商重新谈判。

segments.src: You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
segments.tr: 你无法与衰退重新谈判。

segments.src: The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: 实际的举措是将两层都转化为可行的东西，这就是**SWOT**所做的。

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: 上一行是关于你的——你公司内部的东西。

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: 下一行是关于世界的——它外部的东西。

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: 内部/外部的划分是人们最常搞错的部分。

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).
segments.tr: "我们的品牌广为人知"是一个优势（内部）。

segments.src: "Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: "Z世代饮酒量下降"是一个机会或威胁（外部），而不是劣势，无论伤害有多大。

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.
segments.tr: SWOT的真正价值不在于列表。

segments.src: It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: 这是配对：将优势与机会相匹配，你就找到了一个战略。

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: 发现一个直接位于威胁下方的劣势，你就找到了会让你陷入麻烦的东西。

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.
segments.tr: 想象一下过去十年在得克萨斯州和亚利桑那州郊区蔓延的汽车穿梭咖啡连锁店。

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **政治/法律**——多个州的最低工资底线上升，推高每家店的劳动力成本

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites
segments.tr: - **经济**——当通货膨胀来临时，6美元的拿铁从预算中被削减的速度比杂货快

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one
segments.tr: - **社会**——远程和混合工作摧毁了市区上午8点的办公室高峰，但创造了郊区晚上午时间的高峰

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster
segments.tr: - **技术**——移动订购应用程序让客户在到达前支付，所以队伍移动得更快

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: 现在是微观环境：他们的客户是通勤者和远程工作者，他们的竞争对手是星巴克和每家销售不错冷滴的加油站，他们的供应商是受到波动豆价影响的咖啡进口商。

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **优势：** 小占地面积的店铺、没有就餐区、低租金、快速吞吐量

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.

segments.src: The environment analysis is what decides where the building goes.

segments.src: 1. The macro environment (PEST: political, economic, social, technological) is the weather you can't control; the micro environment (customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, your own company) is close enough to influence.
segments.tr: 1. 宏观环境（PEST：政治、经济、社会、技术）是你无法控制的"天气"；微观环境（客户、竞争对手、供应商、分销商、你自己的公司）足够接近可以影响。

segments.src: 2. SWOT sorts what you found into internal factors (strengths, weaknesses) and external factors (opportunities, threats) — mixing up those two rows is the most common mistake.
segments.tr: 2. SWOT将你发现的东西分类为内部因素（优势、劣势）和外部因素（机会、威胁）——混淆这两行是最常见的错误。

segments.src: 3. A SWOT list is only useful when you pair the cells: strength + opportunity points to a strategy, weakness + threat points to a risk you need to close.
segments.tr: 3. SWOT列表只有在你配对单元格时才有用：优势+机会指向一个战略，劣势+威胁指向你需要关闭的风险。

segments.tr: **2.** 利率上升使客户延迟大额购买是哪一层的一部分，以及PEST中的哪一个字母？

segments.src: - **Macro environment** — broad, society-wide forces (political, economic, social, technological) that affect all firms in an industry and can't be controlled by any one of them.
segments.tr: - **宏观环境** ——广泛的、社会范围的力量（政治、经济、社会、技术），影响行业中的所有公司，不能被其中任何一个控制。

segments.src: - **Micro environment** — the actors closest to the firm — customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, and the company's own resources — that it can influence but not fully control.
segments.tr: - **微观环境** ——离公司最近的参与者——客户、竞争对手、供应商、分销商和公司自己的资源——它可以影响但不能完全控制。

segments.src: - **PEST / PESTEL** — a checklist for scanning the macro environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological (plus Environmental and Legal in the PESTEL version).
segments.tr: - **PEST/PESTEL** ——扫描宏观环境的检查清单：政治、经济、社会、技术（在PESTEL版本中加上环境和法律）。

segments.src: - **SWOT analysis** — a 2x2 framework sorting internal Strengths and Weaknesses against external Opportunities and Threats to turn environmental scanning into strategy.
segments.tr: - **SWOT分析** ——一个2x2框架，将内部优势和劣势与外部机会和威胁进行排序，将环境扫描转化为战略。

segments.src: - **Environmental scanning** — the ongoing practice of gathering and interpreting information about outside forces, so changes are spotted early rather than after they hit revenue.
segments.tr: - **环境扫描** ——持续收集和解释关于外部力量信息的做法，这样变化可以尽早被发现，而不是在它们冲击收入之后。

segments.src: The baker is a resource inside the company, so it's internal and helpful — a strength.
segments.tr: 面包师是公司内部的资源，所以是内部和有利的——优势。

segments.src: Interest rates are a broad force no single bakery or retailer controls, which makes them macro, and they're the "E" in PEST.
segments.tr: 利率是单个面包店或零售商无法控制的广泛力量，这使它们成为宏观，它们是PEST中的"E"。

segments.src: A supplier is a specific party you deal with, negotiate with, and can switch — that's the micro environment.
segments.tr: 供应商是你打交道、谈判和可以切换的特定方，这是微观环境。

segments.src: The macro version of the same problem would be industry-wide commodity inflation.*

hi.title: [Marketing 101 #2] आपका उत्पाद विफल नहीं हुआ — मौसम ने किया

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > किसी भी चीज़ का विपणन करने से पहले, आपको माहौल समझना होगा: वे ताकतें जिन्हें आप नियंत्रित नहीं कर सकते (व्यापक वातावरण), खिलाड़ी जिनके साथ आप दैनिक रूप से व्यवहार करते हैं (सूक्ष्म वातावरण), और एक सरल ग्रिड जो दोनों को निर्णयों में बदल देता है।

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: पिछले पाठ में, विपणन एक विशेष ग्राहक के लिए मूल्य बनाने के बारे में था।

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: लेकिन कोई भी कंपनी एक शून्य में मूल्य नहीं बनाती।

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: हर व्यवसाय एक मौसम प्रणाली के अंदर बैठता है जिसे उसने चुना नहीं।

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: विपणनकर्ता उस मौसम को दो परतों में विभाजित करते हैं।

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **व्यापक वातावरण** बड़ी चीज़ें हैं — समाज-व्यापी ताकतें जो आपके उद्योग में हर कंपनी को एक साथ प्रभावित करती हैं।

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: आप उनके साथ बातचीत नहीं कर सकते; आप केवल उन्हें आते हुए देख सकते हैं।

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **राजनीतिक / कानूनी** — नियम, टैरिफ, न्यूनतम मजदूरी कानून, डेटा गोपनीयता नियम

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **आर्थिक** — ब्याज दरें, मुद्रास्फीति, बेरोजगारी, उपभोक्ता आत्मविश्वास

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **सामाजिक / सांस्कृतिक** — जनसांख्यिकी, मूल्य, आदतें, लोग क्या सामान्य पाते हैं

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **तकनीकी** — नई उपकरण जो बदलते हैं कि चीजें कैसे बनाई जाती हैं, बेची जाती हैं, या डिलीवर की जाती हैं

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: आप **PESTEL** भी देखेंगे, जो पर्यावरणीय और कानूनी को अपनी श्रेणियों के रूप में जोड़ता है।

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.
segments.tr: **सूक्ष्म वातावरण** वह सामग्री है जो छूने के लिए काफी करीब है: आपके ग्राहक, आपके प्रतियोगी, आपके आपूर्तिकर्ता, आपके वितरक, और आपकी अपनी आंतरिक क्षमताएं।

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.
segments.tr: आप अभी भी इन पर पूरी तरह से नियंत्रण नहीं रखते, लेकिन आप उन्हें प्रभावित कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.
segments.tr: आप एक आपूर्तिकर्ता के साथ फिर से बातचीत कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
segments.tr: आप एक मंदी के साथ फिर से बातचीत नहीं कर सकते।

segments.src: The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: व्यावहारिक कदम दोनों परतों को कुछ कार्यान्वयन योग्य में अनुवाद करना है, और यह वही है जो **SWOT** करता है।

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: शीर्ष पंक्ति आपके बारे में है — आपकी कंपनी के अंदर की चीजें।

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: निचली पंक्ति दुनिया के बारे में है — बाहर की चीजें।

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: वह आंतरिक/बाहरी विभाजन वह हिस्सा है जो लोग सबसे अक्सर गलत समझते हैं।

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).
segments.tr: "हमारा ब्रांड अच्छी तरह से जाना जाता है" एक शक्ति (आंतरिक) है।

segments.src: "Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: "जेन जेड कम शराब पी रहा है" एक अवसर या खतरा (बाहरी) है, कमजोरी नहीं, चाहे यह कितना भी नुकसान पहुंचाए।

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.
segments.tr: SWOT का वास्तविक मूल्य सूची नहीं है।

segments.src: It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: यह जोड़ी है: एक शक्ति को एक अवसर से मेल खाएं और आपको एक रणनीति मिल गई है।

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: एक कमजोरी को एक खतरे के सीधे नीचे खोजें और आपको वह चीज़ मिल गई है जो आपको परेशानी में डालेगी।

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.
segments.tr: ड्राइव-थ्रू कॉफी चेनों के बारे में सोचें जो पिछले दशक में उपनगरीय टेक्सास और एरिज़ोना में फैल गई हैं।

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **राजनीतिक/कानूनी** — कई राज्यों में न्यूनतम मजदूरी की सीमा बढ़ी, प्रति स्टोर श्रम लागत को बढ़ाया

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites
segments.tr: - **आर्थिक** — जब मुद्रास्फीति काटती है, तो एक $6 लैट्टे को किराने की चीज़ों की तुलना में बजट से तेजी से काट दिया जाता है

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one
segments.tr: - **सामाजिक** — दूरस्थ और हाइब्रिड काम ने डाउनटाउन में सुबह 8 बजे की कार्यालय की भीड़ को समाप्त कर दिया, लेकिन उपनगरीय देर सुबह की भीड़ बनाई

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster
segments.tr: - **तकनीकी** — मोबाइल ऑर्डरिंग ऐप्स ग्राहकों को आने से पहले भुगतान करने देते हैं, इसलिए लाइन तेजी से चलती है

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: अब सूक्ष्म वातावरण: उनके ग्राहक कम्यूटर और दूरस्थ कर्मचारी हैं, उनके प्रतियोगी स्टारबक्स और हर गैस स्टेशन जो अच्छी ठंडी कॉफी बेचते हैं, उनके आपूर्तिकर्ता कॉफी आयातक हैं जो अस्थिर बीन की कीमतों से प्रभावित हैं।

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **शक्ति:** छोटे स्टोर, कोई डाइनिंग रूम नहीं, कम किराया, तेजी से थ्रूपुट

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything
segments.tr: - **कमजोरी:** लगभग कोई चलना-फिरना या "बैठना और काम करना" व्यवसाय नहीं, इसलिए एक ग्राहक प्रकार सब कुछ ले जाता है

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run
segments.tr: - **अवसर:** उपनगरीय कार-निर्भर पड़ोस जहां दूरस्थ कर्मचारी अभी भी मध्य-सुबह कॉफी रन चाहते हैं

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu
segments.tr: - **खतरा:** कॉफी बीन की कीमत में वृद्धि और बढ़ती मजदूरी कम कीमत वाले मेनू को दबा रही है

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.
segments.tr: उन्हें जोड़ी दें और रणनीति खुद लिख देगी: आवासीय समूहों के पास उपनगरीय स्ट्रिप मॉल में छोटे स्टोर रखें, डाउनटाउन में नहीं।

segments.src: That's a strength meeting an opportunity.
segments.tr: यह एक अवसर से मिलने वाली एक शक्ति है।

segments.src: Meanwhile, the weakness-under-threat combo tells you what to fix — build a loyalty app or a subscription so you're not repricing the menu every time coffee futures jump.
segments.tr: इस बीच, कमजोरी-खतरे का संयोजन आपको बताता है कि क्या ठीक करना है — एक वफादारी ऐप या सदस्यता बनाएं ताकि आप हर बार कॉफी वायदा कूदने पर कीमतें फिर से तय न करें।
एक जैसी कॉफी, एक जैसे बीन।

segments.tr: वातावरण विश्लेषण यह तय करता है कि भवन कहाँ जाता है।

segments.src: **2.** Rising interest rates making customers delay big purchases is part of which layer, and which PEST letter?
segments.tr: **2.** बढ़ती ब्याज दरें जो ग्राहकों को बड़ी खरीद में देरी करने के लिए प्रेरित करती हैं, किस परत का हिस्सा है, और किस PEST अक्षर का?

segments.tr: - **सूक्ष्म वातावरण** — फर्म के सबसे करीब के अभिनेता — ग्राहक, प्रतियोगी, आपूर्तिकर्ता, वितरक, और कंपनी के अपने संसाधन — जिन्हें यह प्रभावित कर सकता है लेकिन पूरी तरह से नियंत्रित नहीं कर सकता।

segments.src: - **PEST / PESTEL** — a checklist for scanning the macro environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological (plus Environmental and Legal in the PESTEL version).

segments.src: - **SWOT analysis** — a 2x2 framework sorting internal Strengths and Weaknesses against external Opportunities and Threats to turn environmental scanning into strategy.
segments.tr: - **SWOT विश्लेषण** — एक 2x2 ढांचा जो आंतरिक शक्तियों और कमजोरियों को बाहरी अवसरों और खतरों के विरुद्ध क्रमबद्ध करता है ताकि पर्यावरणीय स्कैनिंग को रणनीति में बदल दिया जाए।

segments.src: - **Environmental scanning** — the ongoing practice of gathering and interpreting information about outside forces, so changes are spotted early rather than after they hit revenue.
segments.tr: - **पर्यावरणीय स्कैनिंग** — बाहरी ताकतों के बारे में जानकारी एकत्र करने और व्याख्या करने की चल रहा अभ्यास, ताकि परिवर्तन जल्दी खोजे जाएं न कि राजस्व को प्रभावित करने के बाद।

segments.src: The baker is a resource inside the company, so it's internal and helpful — a strength.

es.title: [Marketing 101 #2] Tu Producto No Fracasó — El Clima Lo Hizo

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > Antes de poder vender algo, tienes que leer la sala: las fuerzas que no puedes controlar (el macro entorno), los jugadores con los que tratas a diario (el micro entorno), y una cuadrícula simple que convierte ambos en decisiones.

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: En la lección anterior, el marketing se trataba de crear valor para un cliente específico.

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: Pero ninguna empresa crea valor en el vacío.

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: Todo negocio se sienta dentro de un sistema climático que no eligió.

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: Los profesionales del marketing dividen ese clima en dos capas.

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **El macro entorno** es lo grande — fuerzas a nivel de la sociedad que afectan a todas las empresas de tu industria a la vez.

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: No puedes negociar con ellas; solo puedes verlas llegar.
La lista de verificación estándar es **PEST**:

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **Político / legal** — regulaciones, aranceles, leyes de salario mínimo, reglas de privacidad de datos

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **Económico** — tasas de interés, inflación, desempleo, confianza del consumidor

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **Social / cultural** — demografía, valores, hábitos, lo que la gente considera normal

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **Tecnológico** — nuevas herramientas que cambian cómo se hacen, venden o entregan las cosas

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: También verás **PESTEL**, que añade Ambiental y Legal como sus propias categorías.

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.
segments.tr: **El micro entorno** es lo suficientemente cercano para tocar: tus clientes, tus competidores, tus proveedores, tus distribuidores, y tus propias capacidades internas.

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.
segments.tr: Aún no controlas completamente estos, pero puedes influir en ellos.

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.
You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
segments.tr: No puedes renegociar con una recesión.

segments.src: The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: El movimiento práctico es traducir ambas capas en algo accionable, y eso es lo que hace **SWOT**.

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: La fila superior se trata de ti — cosas dentro de tu empresa.

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: La fila inferior se trata del mundo — cosas fuera de él.

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: Esa división interna/externa es la parte que las personas cometen mal más a menudo.

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).
segments.tr: "Nuestra marca es bien conocida" es una fortaleza (interna).

segments.src: "Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: "La Gen Z está bebiendo menos alcohol" es una oportunidad o amenaza (externa), no una debilidad, sin importar cuánto duela.

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.
segments.tr: El valor real de SWOT no es la lista.

segments.src: It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: Es el emparejamiento: empareja una fortaleza con una oportunidad y habrás encontrado una estrategia.

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: Identifica una debilidad directamente bajo una amenaza y habrás encontrado lo que te meterá en problemas.

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.
segments.tr: Piensa en las cadenas de café de paso que se extendieron por el Texas y Arizona suburbano durante la década pasada.

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **Político/legal** — los pisos de salario mínimo subieron en varios estados, empujando los costos de mano de obra por tienda

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites
segments.tr: - **Económico** — un café de $6 se corta del presupuesto más rápido que los comestibles cuando la inflación muerde

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one
segments.tr: - **Social** — el trabajo remoto e híbrido aniquiló la prisa de oficina del centro a las 8 a.m., pero creó una a última hora de la mañana en los suburbios

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster
segments.tr: - **Tecnológico** — las aplicaciones de pedidos móviles permiten que los clientes paguen antes de llegar, por lo que la línea se mueve más rápido

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: Ahora el micro entorno: sus clientes son viajeros y trabajadores remotos, sus competidores son Starbucks y todas las gasolineras que venden café frío decente, sus proveedores son importadores de café afectados por precios de granos volátiles.

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **Fortaleza:** tiendas de huella pequeña, sin comedor, renta baja, alto rendimiento

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything
segments.tr: - **Debilidad:** casi ningún negocio de entrada libre o "siéntate y trabaja", entonces un tipo de cliente carga todo

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run
segments.tr: - **Oportunidad:** barrios suburbanos dependientes de automóviles donde los trabajadores remotos aún quieren una parada de café a media mañana

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu
segments.tr: - **Amenaza:** picos de precios de granos de café y salarios crecientes apretando un menú de bajo precio

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.
segments.tr: Empareja los y la estrategia se escribe por sí sola: pon pequeñas tiendas en centros comerciales de tiras suburbanas cerca de clusters residenciales, no en el centro.

segments.src: That's a strength meeting an opportunity.
segments.tr: Eso es una fortaleza encontrando una oportunidad.

segments.src: Meanwhile, the weakness-under-threat combo tells you what to fix — build a loyalty app or a subscription so you're not repricing the menu every time coffee futures jump.
segments.tr: Mientras tanto, la combinación debilidad-bajo-amenaza te dice qué arreglar — construye una aplicación de lealtad o una suscripción para que no estés revaluando el menú cada vez que los futuros del café suban.

segments.src: The environment analysis is what decides where the building goes.
segments.tr: El análisis del entorno es lo que decide dónde va el edificio.

segments.src: 1. The macro environment (PEST: political, economic, social, technological) is the weather you can't control; the micro environment (customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, your own company) is close enough to influence.
segments.tr: 1. El macro entorno (PEST: político, económico, social, tecnológico) es el clima que no puedes controlar; el micro entorno (clientes, competidores, proveedores, distribuidores, tu propia empresa) está lo suficientemente cerca para influir.

segments.src: 2. SWOT sorts what you found into internal factors (strengths, weaknesses) and external factors (opportunities, threats) — mixing up those two rows is the most common mistake.
segments.tr: 2. SWOT clasifica lo que encontraste en factores internos (fortalezas, debilidades) y factores externos (oportunidades, amenazas) — mezclar esas dos filas es el error más común.

segments.src: 3. A SWOT list is only useful when you pair the cells: strength + opportunity points to a strategy, weakness + threat points to a risk you need to close.
segments.tr: 3. Una lista de SWOT es solo útil cuando emparejas las celdas: fortaleza + oportunidad apunta a una estrategia, debilidad + amenaza apunta a un riesgo que necesitas cerrar.

segments.tr: **1.** Una panadería anota: "Nuestro panadero jefe tiene 20 años de experiencia."

segments.tr: En un análisis SWOT, esto pertenece a —

segments.tr: **2.** Los tipos de interés en aumento que hacen que los clientes retrasen grandes compras es parte de qué capa, y qué letra de PEST?

segments.src: **3.** O/X: Your main supplier raising prices is part of the macro environment.
segments.tr: **3.** V/F: Tu proveedor principal aumentando precios es parte del macro entorno.

fr.title: [Marketing 101 #2] Votre Produit N'a Pas Échoué — C'est la Météo

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > Avant de pouvoir commercialiser quoi que ce soit, vous devez lire la salle : les forces que vous ne pouvez pas contrôler (l'environnement macroéconomique), les acteurs avec lesquels vous traitez quotidiennement (l'environnement microéconomique), et une grille simple qui transforme les deux en décisions.

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: Dans la dernière leçon, le marketing parlait de créer de la valeur pour un client spécifique.

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: Mais aucune entreprise ne crée de la valeur dans le vide.

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: Chaque entreprise se trouve à l'intérieur d'un système météorologique qu'elle n'a pas choisi.

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: Les spécialistes du marketing divisent cette météorologie en deux couches.

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **L'environnement macroéconomique** est la grande affaire — les forces à l'échelle de la société qui affectent chaque entreprise de votre industrie à la fois.

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: Vous ne pouvez pas négocier avec elles ; vous pouvez seulement les voir venir.
La liste de contrôle standard est **PEST** :

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **Politique / juridique** — réglementations, tarifs, lois de salaire minimum, règles de confidentialité des données

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **Économique** — taux d'intérêt, inflation, chômage, confiance des consommateurs

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **Social / culturel** — démographie, valeurs, habitudes, ce que les gens trouvent normal

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **Technologique** — nouveaux outils qui changent la façon dont les choses sont fabriquées, vendues ou livrées

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: Vous verrez aussi **PESTEL**, qui ajoute Environnemental et Juridique comme leurs propres catégories.

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.
segments.tr: **L'environnement microéconomique** est ce qui est assez proche pour le toucher : vos clients, vos concurrents, vos fournisseurs, vos distributeurs, et vos propres capacités internes.

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.
segments.tr: Vous ne les contrôlez toujours pas complètement, mais vous pouvez les influencer.

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.
segments.tr: Vous pouvez renégocier avec un fournisseur.

segments.src: You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
segments.tr: Vous ne pouvez pas renégocier avec une récession.

segments.src: The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: Le mouvement pratique est de traduire les deux couches en quelque chose d'actionnable, et c'est ce que **SWOT** fait.

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: La ligne supérieure est à propos de vous — les choses à l'intérieur de votre entreprise.

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: La ligne inférieure est à propos du monde — les choses en dehors de celui-ci.

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: Ce partage interne/externe est la partie que les gens confondent le plus souvent.

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).
segments.tr: « Notre marque est bien connue » est une force (interne).

segments.src: "Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: « La Gen Z boit moins d'alcool » est une opportunité ou une menace (externe), pas une faiblesse, peu importe à quel point cela fait mal.

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.
segments.tr: La vraie valeur de SWOT n'est pas la liste.

segments.src: It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: C'est l'appariement : associez une force à une opportunité et vous avez trouvé une stratégie.

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: Repérez une faiblesse assise directement sous une menace et vous avez trouvé la chose qui vous mettra en difficulté.

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.
segments.tr: Pensez aux chaînes de cafés drive-thru qui se sont propagées dans la région suburbaine du Texas et de l'Arizona au cours de la dernière décennie.

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **Politique/juridique** — les salaires minima ont augmenté dans plusieurs États, augmentant les coûts de main-d'œuvre par magasin

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites
segments.tr: - **Économique** — un café latté à $6 est coupé du budget plus rapidement que l'épicerie quand l'inflation frappe

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one
segments.tr: - **Social** — le travail à distance et hybride a anéanti l'afflux de 8 h du matin au centre-ville, mais a créé un en fin de matinée en banlieue

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster
segments.tr: - **Technologique** — les applications de commande mobile permettent aux clients de payer avant leur arrivée, de sorte que la ligne se déplace plus rapidement

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: Maintenant l'environnement micro : leurs clients sont des navetteurs et des travailleurs à distance, leurs concurrents sont Starbucks et chaque station-service vendant du bon café froid, leurs fournisseurs sont des importateurs de café touchés par les prix volatiles des grains.

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **Force** : petits magasins, pas de salle à manger, loyer bas, débit rapide

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything
segments.tr: - **Faiblesse** : presque pas de commerce de passage ou « assis et travail », donc un type de client porte tout

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run
segments.tr: - **Opportunité** : quartiers de banlieue dépendants des automobiles où les travailleurs à distance veulent toujours une pause-café en milieu de matinée

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu
segments.tr: - **Menace** : les pics de prix des grains de café et les salaires croissants comprimant un menu à bas prix

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.
segments.tr: Associez-les et la stratégie s'écrit d'elle-même : mettez de petits magasins dans les centres commerciaux de banlieue près des grappes résidentielles, pas au centre-ville.

segments.src: That's a strength meeting an opportunity.
segments.tr: C'est une force rencontrant une opportunité.

segments.src: Meanwhile, the weakness-under-threat combo tells you what to fix — build a loyalty app or a subscription so you're not repricing the menu every time coffee futures jump.
segments.tr: Pendant ce temps, la combinaison faiblesse-sous-menace vous dit ce qu'il faut corriger — créez une application de fidélité ou un abonnement pour ne pas avoir à revoir les prix du menu chaque fois que les contrats à terme du café augmentent.

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > Sebelum Anda dapat memasarkan apa pun, Anda harus membaca ruangan: kekuatan yang tidak dapat Anda kontrol (lingkungan makro), pemain yang Anda hadapi setiap hari (lingkungan mikro), dan grid sederhana yang mengubah keduanya menjadi keputusan.

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: Dalam pelajaran terakhir, pemasaran adalah tentang menciptakan nilai bagi pelanggan tertentu.

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: Tetapi tidak ada perusahaan yang menciptakan nilai dalam ruang hampa.

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: Setiap bisnis berada di dalam sistem cuaca yang tidak dipilihnya.

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: Pemasar membagi cuaca itu menjadi dua lapisan.

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **Lingkungan makro** adalah hal-hal besar — kekuatan yang mencakup seluruh masyarakat yang mempengaruhi setiap perusahaan di industri Anda sekaligus.

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: Anda tidak dapat bernegosiasi dengan mereka; Anda hanya dapat melihat mereka datang.

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **Politik / hukum** — regulasi, tarif, undang-undang upah minimum, aturan privasi data

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **Ekonomi** — suku bunga, inflasi, pengangguran, kepercayaan konsumen

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **Sosial / budaya** — demografi, nilai-nilai, kebiasaan, apa yang dianggap orang wajar

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **Teknologi** — alat baru yang mengubah cara barang dibuat, dijual, atau dikirimkan

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: Anda juga akan melihat **PESTEL**, yang menambahkan Lingkungan dan Hukum sebagai kategori mereka sendiri.
Ide yang sama, potongan yang lebih halus.

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.

標準的なチェックリストは**PEST**です：

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **経済** — 金利、インフレーション、失業、消費者信頼感

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **社会・文化** — 人口統計、価値観、習慣、人々が正常と思うもの

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **技術** — 物がどのように製造・販売・配送されるかを変える新しいツール

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.

segments.src: You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
segments.tr: リセッションと再交渉することはできません。

segments.src: The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: 実践的な手段は、両方の層を実行可能なものに変換することです。それが**SWOT**がすることです。

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: 上の行はあなたについて——企業内のもの。

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: 下の行は世界について——その外のもの。

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: この内部/外部の分割は、人々が最も頻繁に間違える部分です。

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).

segments.src: "Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: 「Gen Zはアルコール消費量を減らしている」は機会または脅威です（外部）。弱みではありません。どんなにひどい痛手を受けたとしても。

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.

segments.src: It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: ペアリングです：強みと機会をマッチさせれば、戦略が見つかります。

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: 脅威のすぐ下に直接位置している弱みを見つければ、あなたを困らせるリスクが見つかります。

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.

これらにPESTを当てはめます：

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **政治・法律** — 複数の州で最低賃金が上昇し、1店舗あたりの人件費が上昇しました

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: 次にミクロ環境です：顧客は通勤者とリモートワーカー、競合他社はスターバックスと質の良いコールドブリューを売っているすべてのガソリンスタンド、サプライヤーは豆の価格変動に打撃を受けたコーヒー輸入業者です。

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **強み：** 小さいフットプリントの店、食事ルームなし、低家賃、高速スループット

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything
segments.tr: - **弱み：** ほぼ立ち寄りや「座って仕事」ビジネスがないため、1つの顧客タイプがすべてを支えています

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run
segments.tr: - **機会：** リモートワーカーが午前中盤のコーヒー購入を求める郊外の車依存地域

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu
segments.tr: - **脅威：** コーヒー豆の価格急騰と賃金上昇が低価格メニューを圧迫しています

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.

segments.src: That's a strength meeting an opportunity.
segments.tr: それは強みが機会と出会っています。

segments.src: Meanwhile, the weakness-under-threat combo tells you what to fix — build a loyalty app or a subscription so you're not repricing the menu every time coffee futures jump.
segments.tr: 一方、弱み-脅威コンボはあなたが修正する必要があることを示しています——ロイヤリティアプリまたはサブスクリプションを構築して、コーヒー先物が上昇するたびにメニューを再価格設定しないようにします。

segments.tr: Zinssätze sind eine breite Kraft, die keine einzelne Bäckerei oder kein Einzelhandelsgeschäft kontrolliert, weshalb sie makro sind, und sie sind das "E" in PEST.

segments.src: A supplier is a specific party you deal with, negotiate with, and can switch — that's the micro environment.
segments.tr: Ein Lieferant ist eine spezifische Partei, mit der du umgehen, verhandeln und wechseln kannst — das ist die Mikroumgebung.

segments.src: The macro version of the same problem would be industry-wide commodity inflation.*
segments.tr: Die Makroversion desselben Problems wäre branchenweite Rohstoff-Inflation.*

vi.title: [Marketing 101 #2] Sản Phẩm Của Bạn Không Thất Bại — Là Do Thời Tiết

segments.src: > Before you can market anything, you have to read the room: the forces you can't control (the macro environment), the players you deal with daily (the micro environment), and a simple grid that turns both into decisions.
segments.tr: > Trước khi bạn có thể tiếp thị bất cứ điều gì, bạn phải hiểu rõ tình hình: những lực lượng bạn không thể kiểm soát (môi trường vĩ mô), những bên bạn giao dịch hàng ngày (môi trường vi mô), và một lưới đơn giản biến cả hai thành quyết định.

segments.src: In the last lesson, marketing was about creating value for a specific customer.
segments.tr: Trong bài học trước, tiếp thị là về tạo giá trị cho một khách hàng cụ thể.

segments.src: But no company creates value in a vacuum.
segments.tr: Nhưng không có công ty nào tạo giá trị trong chân không.

segments.src: Every business sits inside a weather system it didn't choose.
segments.tr: Mỗi doanh nghiệp đều nằm bên trong một hệ thống thời tiết mà nó không chọn lựa.

segments.src: Marketers split that weather into two layers.
segments.tr: Các nhà tiếp thị chia "thời tiết" đó thành hai lớp.

segments.src: **The macro environment** is the big stuff — society-wide forces that affect every company in your industry at once.
segments.tr: **Môi trường vĩ mô** là những vấn đề lớn — những lực lượng toàn xã hội ảnh hưởng đến mọi công ty trong ngành của bạn cùng một lúc.

segments.src: You cannot negotiate with them; you can only see them coming.
segments.tr: Bạn không thể thương lượng với chúng; bạn chỉ có thể thấy chúng sắp tới.
Danh sách kiểm tra tiêu chuẩn là **PEST**:

segments.src: - **Political / legal** — regulations, tariffs, minimum wage laws, data privacy rules
segments.tr: - **Chính trị / Pháp lý** — các quy định, thuế quan, luật lương tối thiểu, quy tắc bảo vệ dữ liệu

segments.src: - **Economic** — interest rates, inflation, unemployment, consumer confidence
segments.tr: - **Kinh tế** — lãi suất, lạm phát, thất nghiệp, niềm tin của người tiêu dùng

segments.src: - **Social / cultural** — demographics, values, habits, what people find normal
segments.tr: - **Xã hội / Văn hóa** — nhân khẩu học, giá trị, thói quen, những gì mọi người coi là bình thường

segments.src: - **Technological** — new tools that change how things get made, sold, or delivered
segments.tr: - **Công nghệ** — những công cụ mới thay đổi cách sản xuất, bán hàng hoặc giao hàng

segments.src: You'll also see **PESTEL**, which adds Environmental and Legal as their own categories.
segments.tr: Bạn cũng sẽ thấy **PESTEL**, thêm Môi trường và Pháp lý làm các danh mục riêng của chúng.
Cùng ý tưởng, chia thành những phần nhỏ hơn.

segments.src: **The micro environment** is the stuff close enough to touch: your customers, your competitors, your suppliers, your distributors, and your own internal capabilities.
segments.tr: **Môi trường vi mô** là những thứ gần đủ để chạm vào: khách hàng của bạn, đối thủ cạnh tranh của bạn, nhà cung cấp của bạn, các nhà phân phối của bạn, và khả năng nội bộ của riêng bạn.

segments.src: You still don't fully control these, but you can influence them.
segments.tr: Bạn vẫn không hoàn toàn kiểm soát những thứ này, nhưng bạn có thể ảnh hưởng đến chúng.

segments.src: You can renegotiate with a supplier.
segments.tr: Bạn có thể tái thương lượng với một nhà cung cấp.

segments.src: You cannot renegotiate with a recession.
segments.tr: Bạn không thể tái thương lượng với một cuộc suy thoái.

segments.src: The practical move is to translate both layers into something actionable, and that's what **SWOT** does.
segments.tr: Bước thực tế là dịch cả hai lớp thành điều gì đó có thể hành động được, và đó là những gì **SWOT** làm.

segments.src: The top row is about you — things inside your company.
segments.tr: Hàng trên là về bạn — những thứ bên trong công ty bạn.

segments.src: The bottom row is about the world — things outside it.
segments.tr: Hàng dưới là về thế giới — những thứ bên ngoài nó.

segments.src: That internal/external split is the part people get wrong most often.
segments.tr: Sự chia tách nội bộ/bên ngoài đó là phần mọi người hiểu sai thường xuyên nhất.

segments.src: "Our brand is well known" is a strength (internal).
segments.tr: "Thương hiệu của chúng tôi rất nổi tiếng" là một sức mạnh (nội bộ).

segments.src: "Gen Z is drinking less alcohol" is an opportunity or threat (external), not a weakness, no matter how badly it hurts.
segments.tr: "Gen Z đang uống ít rượu hơn" là một cơ hội hoặc mối đe dọa (bên ngoài), không phải là một điểm yếu, bất kể nó ảnh hưởng xấu như thế nào.

segments.src: SWOT's real value isn't the list.
segments.tr: Giá trị thực sự của SWOT không phải là danh sách.

segments.src: It's the pairing: match a strength to an opportunity and you've found a strategy.
segments.tr: Đó là sự ghép nối: ghép một sức mạnh với một cơ hội và bạn đã tìm thấy một chiến lược.

segments.src: Spot a weakness sitting directly under a threat and you've found the thing that will get you in trouble.
segments.tr: Phát hiện một điểm yếu nằm trực tiếp dưới một mối đe dọa và bạn đã tìm thấy thứ sẽ gây rắc rối cho bạn.

segments.src: Think about the drive-thru coffee chains that spread across suburban Texas and Arizona over the past decade.
segments.tr: Hãy nghĩ về những chuỗi cà phê drive-thru đã lan rộng khắp ngoại ô Texas và Arizona trong thập kỷ qua.

segments.src: - **Political/legal** — minimum wage floors rose in several states, pushing up labor costs per store
segments.tr: - **Chính trị/Pháp lý** — mức lương tối thiểu tăng lên ở một số tiểu bang, đẩy tăng chi phí lao động trên một cửa hàng

segments.src: - **Economic** — a $6 latte gets cut from the budget faster than groceries when inflation bites
segments.tr: - **Kinh tế** — một ly cà phê $6 bị cắt khỏi ngân sách nhanh hơn các mặt hàng tạp hóa khi lạm phát cắn

segments.src: - **Social** — remote and hybrid work gutted the downtown 8 a.m. office rush, but created a suburban late-morning one
segments.tr: - **Xã hội** — công việc từ xa và kết hợp đã phá hủy sự tấn tấu 8 giờ sáng ở trung tâm thành phố, nhưng tạo ra một sự tấn tấu buổi sáng muộn ở ngoại ô

segments.src: - **Technological** — mobile ordering apps let customers pay before they arrive, so the line moves faster
segments.tr: - **Công nghệ** — các ứng dụng đặt hàng di động cho phép khách hàng thanh toán trước khi họ tới, vì vậy hàng chờ xử lý nhanh hơn

segments.src: Now the micro environment: their customers are commuters and remote workers, their competitors are Starbucks and every gas station selling decent cold brew, their suppliers are coffee importers hit by volatile bean prices.
segments.tr: Bây giờ môi trường vi mô: khách hàng của họ là những người đi lại và người lao động từ xa, đối thủ cạnh tranh của họ là Starbucks và mọi trạm xăng bán cà phê lạnh chất lượng tốt, nhà cung cấp của họ là những người nhập khẩu cà phê bị ảnh hưởng bởi giá đậu cà phê biến động.

segments.src: - **Strength:** small-footprint stores, no dining room, low rent, fast throughput
segments.tr: - **Sức mạnh:** các cửa hàng diện tích nhỏ, không phòng ăn, giá thuê thấp, thông lượng nhanh

segments.src: - **Weakness:** almost no walk-in or "sit and work" business, so one customer type carries everything
segments.tr: - **Điểm yếu:** hầu như không có khách đi vào hoặc kinh doanh "ngồi và làm việc", vì vậy một loại khách hàng mang lại mọi thứ

segments.src: - **Opportunity:** suburban car-dependent neighborhoods where remote workers still want a mid-morning coffee run
segments.tr: - **Cơ hội:** các khu phố ngoại ô phụ thuộc vào ô tô nơi những người lao động từ xa vẫn muốn uống cà phê vào giữa sáng

segments.src: - **Threat:** coffee bean price spikes and rising wages squeezing a low-price menu
segments.tr: - **Đe dọa:** giá đậu cà phê tăng vọt và lương tăng đè nén thực đơn giá thấp

segments.src: Pair them and the strategy writes itself: put small stores in suburban strip malls near residential clusters, not downtown.
segments.tr: Ghép chúng và chiến lược tự viết ra: đặt các cửa hàng nhỏ trong các trung tâm mua sắm dải ngoại ô gần các cụm dân cư, không phải ở trung tâm thành phố.

segments.src: That's a strength meeting an opportunity.
segments.tr: Đó là sức mạnh gặp một cơ hội.

segments.src: Meanwhile, the weakness-under-threat combo tells you what to fix — build a loyalty app or a subscription so you're not repricing the menu every time coffee futures jump.
segments.tr: Trong khi đó, sự kết hợp yếu điểm-dưới-mối đe dọa cho bạn biết cần khắc phục cái gì — xây dựng một ứng dụng giữ khách hoặc một gói đăng ký để bạn không phải thay đổi giá thực đơn mỗi khi giá cà phê tương lai tăng vọt.
Cà phê giống nhau, đậu giống nhau.

segments.src: The environment analysis is what decides where the building goes.
segments.tr: Phân tích môi trường là những gì quyết định nơi xây dựng.

segments.src: 1. The macro environment (PEST: political, economic, social, technological) is the weather you can't control; the micro environment (customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, your own company) is close enough to influence.
segments.tr: 1. Môi trường vĩ mô (PEST: chính trị, kinh tế, xã hội, công nghệ) là thời tiết bạn không thể kiểm soát; môi trường vi mô (khách hàng, đối thủ cạnh tranh, nhà cung cấp, nhà phân phối, công ty của riêng bạn) đủ gần để bạn có thể ảnh hưởng.

segments.src: 2. SWOT sorts what you found into internal factors (strengths, weaknesses) and external factors (opportunities, threats) — mixing up those two rows is the most common mistake.
segments.tr: 2. SWOT phân loại những gì bạn tìm thấy thành các yếu tố nội bộ (sức mạnh, điểm yếu) và các yếu tố bên ngoài (cơ hội, đe dọa) — trộn lẫn hai hàng này là lỗi phổ biến nhất.

segments.src: 3. A SWOT list is only useful when you pair the cells: strength + opportunity points to a strategy, weakness + threat points to a risk you need to close.
segments.tr: 3. Danh sách SWOT chỉ hữu ích khi bạn ghép các ô: sức mạnh + cơ hội chỉ đến một chiến lược, điểm yếu + đe dọa chỉ đến một rủi ro bạn cần khắc phục.

segments.src: **1.** A bakery notes: "Our head baker has 20 years of experience."
segments.tr: **1.** Một tiệm bánh ghi chú: "Người thợ bánh chính của chúng tôi có 20 năm kinh nghiệm."

segments.src: In a SWOT analysis, this belongs in —
segments.tr: Trong phân tích SWOT, cái này thuộc về —

segments.src: **2.** Rising interest rates making customers delay big purchases is part of which layer, and which PEST letter?
segments.tr: **2.** Lãi suất tăng khiến khách hàng trì hoãn những giao dịch mua lớn là một phần của lớp nào, và chữ PEST nào?
- (a) Môi trường vi mô, Xã hội
- (b) Môi trường vĩ mô, Kinh tế
- (c) Môi trường vi mô, Chính trị
- (d) Môi trường vĩ mô, Công nghệ

segments.src: **3.** O/X: Your main supplier raising prices is part of the macro environment.
segments.tr: **3.** Đúng/Sai: Nhà cung cấp chính của bạn tăng giá là một phần của môi trường vĩ mô.

segments.src: - **Macro environment** — broad, society-wide forces (political, economic, social, technological) that affect all firms in an industry and can't be controlled by any one of them.
segments.tr: - **Môi trường vĩ mô** — những lực lượng rộng lớn, toàn xã hội (chính trị, kinh tế, xã hội, công nghệ) ảnh hưởng đến tất cả các công ty trong một ngành và không thể được kiểm soát bởi bất kỳ một trong số chúng.

segments.src: - **Micro environment** — the actors closest to the firm — customers, competitors, suppliers, distributors, and the company's own resources — that it can influence but not fully control.
segments.tr: - **Môi trường vi mô** — các bên tác động gần nhất đến công ty — khách hàng, đối thủ cạnh tranh, nhà cung cấp, các nhà phân phối, và tài nguyên riêng của công ty — mà nó có thể ảnh hưởng nhưng không thể kiểm soát hoàn toàn.

segments.src: - **PEST / PESTEL** — a checklist for scanning the macro environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological (plus Environmental and Legal in the PESTEL version).
segments.tr: - **PEST / PESTEL** — một danh sách kiểm tra để quét môi trường vĩ mô: Chính trị, Kinh tế, Xã hội, Công nghệ (cộng với Môi trường và Pháp lý trong phiên bản PESTEL).

segments.src: - **SWOT analysis** — a 2x2 framework sorting internal Strengths and Weaknesses against external Opportunities and Threats to turn environmental scanning into strategy.
segments.tr: - **Phân tích SWOT** — một khung 2x2 phân loại các Sức mạnh và Điểm yếu nội bộ so với Cơ hội và Đe dọa bên ngoài để biến quét môi trường thành chiến lược.

segments.src: - **Environmental scanning** — the ongoing practice of gathering and interpreting information about outside forces, so changes are spotted early rather than after they hit revenue.
segments.tr: - **Quét môi trường** — thực hành liên tục thu thập và diễn giải thông tin về các lực lượng bên ngoài, để những thay đổi được phát hiện sớm chứ không phải sau khi chúng ảnh hưởng đến doanh thu.

segments.src: The baker is a resource inside the company, so it's internal and helpful — a strength.
segments.tr: Người thợ bánh là một tài nguyên bên trong công ty, vì vậy nó nằm bên trong và hữu ích — một sức mạnh.

segments.src: Interest rates are a broad force no single bakery or retailer controls, which makes them macro, and they're the "E" in PEST.
segments.tr: Lãi suất là một lực lượng rộng lớn mà không có tiệm bánh hoặc nhà bán lẻ nào kiểm soát được, điều này làm cho chúng là vĩ mô, và chúng là "E" trong PEST.

segments.src: A supplier is a specific party you deal with, negotiate with, and can switch — that's the micro environment.
segments.tr: Nhà cung cấp là một bên cụ thể bạn giao dịch, thương lượng, và có thể chuyển đổi — đó là môi trường vi mô.

segments.src: The macro version of the same problem would be industry-wide commodity inflation.*
segments.tr: Phiên bản vĩ mô của cùng một vấn đề sẽ là lạm phát hàng hóa toàn ngành.*
